That number is a low-confidence subjective estimate, not a statistically supported probability; these facts cannot establish whether sex influenced the decision.

An all-male panel warrants scrutiny, but does not itself prove bias. Depending on your jurisdiction, public-sector appointment panels may have gender-balance requirements.

Your leadership qualifications justify asking how candidates were assessed, although the announcement may omit relevant qualifications or interview performance.

Follow up in writing now, requesting the selection criteria, comparative reasoning, and applicable panel-composition rules. Raise the panel’s composition as a procedural question, not an accusation. Preserve correspondence and check complaint deadlines promptly; waiting for an explanation may not pause them.
